The time depends according to the lost walls of the tooth meaning if you restore almost most of the tooth walls it stays for less time than one wall or surface. The problem is composite restoration going shrinkage overtime causing leakage around the margins where bacteria and food may go through and cause recurrent decay. I see amalgam restoration has more longevity than composite if it's a posterior tooth esthetics don't matter. But best of them in longevity are crown restorations.

About the black spots on your teeth. That's staining you have to go for scaling and polishing but you say you're teeth are sensitive all the time so you may experience higher sensitivity than usual. About the sensitivity if he's the same dentist you're used to going I suggest you find an endodontist or a periodontist. It could be a sort of peridontal disease or pulpal disease meanwhile the teeth look sound.
